The duration of the cell cycle varies from one species to another and from one cell type to another. The G1 phase varies the most. For example, embryonic cells can pass through the G1 phase so quickly that it hardly exists, whereas neurons are arrested in the cell cycle and do not divide.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The question asks for the earliest observable event in prophase in mammalian cells. By the textbook definition, prophase begins when chromatin condenses enough to become visible as chromosomes. Therefore, the first sign of prophase is the appearance of chromosomes.
